messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to pick an approach for per-customer span isolation before next week's infra freeze. Two options on the table:
1) Collector-level routing -> dedicated exporters / sinks per-customer (S3 prefix / kafka topic per-tenant)
2) Single pipeline with tenant tags and downstream split/retention.
Pros/cons: compliance & RBAC are easier with separate datasets, but ops cost and exporter count explode. Thoughts?

Chris: leaning toward separate datasets for regulated customers. makes audits + IAM much simpler. downside = S3 bucket/partition explosion + harder global queries. :thinking_face:

Joel: agree with compromise: hybrid model. route small customers into a shared namespace with strong tenant tagging; route high-volume or regulated customers to dedicated exporters. that keeps # of exporters bounded while preserving per-customer isolation where it matters.

Sara: retention/enforcement is a huge part of this. If we do per-customer buckets we can apply lifecycle rules (30/90/365) easily. With shared buckets we'd need to enforce retention at query layer or add object tagging + lifecycle rule per-tag which is ugly for S3. Also billing tags must flow through exporters.

Priya: console UX/RBAC note — customers and CSMs need simple "view spans for customer X" with audit logs. If we rely on tags only, querying in the console will need a tenant-aware query layer and RBAC checks on every request. With per-customer datasets we can map console roles to dataset ACLs which is simpler.

Chris: Question on implementation complexity — OTEL collector supports routing processor. can we keep a small number of collector configs and route via attributes? Example routing snippet I pasted a while ago: 
```yaml
processors:
  routing:
    table:
      - match:
          attributes:
            customer_id: "cust-123"
        exporters: [s3/cust-123]
      - match:
          attributes:
            customer_tier: "enterprise"
        exporters: [kafka/enterprise, s3/enterprise]
      - match:
          exporters: [s3/shared]
```
This lets us avoid one collector per customer.

Joel: yes that router is the key. but two caveats:
- attribute extraction must be done reliably at ingress (api gateway or SDK) or we'll misroute
- scaling exporters: kafka topics vs S3 prefixes behave differently for retention and access controls

Maya: good points. On RBAC: propose we enforce two controls: 1) management plane mapping (who can create dataset X) + 2) runtime enforcement (console queries check dataset ACL). That works with both designs but is simpler with separate datasets.

Priya: +1. For console we can surface a "dataset selector" when viewing telemetry and default to the tenant context. Also need an admin view to perform cross-tenant debugging for SREs — gated by a special role.

Sara: cost note — S3 object count/PUT costs for many small files could spike. recommend bundling spans into time-windowed files (5m) at the exporter and gzipping before upload. Also consider warm-shard topics in Kafka for heavy tenants.

Maya: action items:
- Joel -> POC routing table + attribute extraction in collector (deploy to staging) (owner: Joel)
- Chris -> cost model for per-customer S3 vs shared+tagging (owner: Chris)
- Priya -> console RBAC mapping doc & UX sketches for dataset selector (owner: Priya)
- Sara -> retention lifecycle patterns + S3 export batching guidance (owner: Sara)

Joel: I'll start with a minimal collector config and a fake SDK header for attributes. Expect a demo by EOD Wednesday.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: collector-routing-staging -> started (build 54321). logs: "failed to mount secret otel-keys" — rolling back.

Maya: thanks — keep updates here. if infra-bot keeps failing, can someone pick secret ownership? @Chris? :+1:

Chris: grabbing ownership now, will rotate secret and re-run.

Priya: leaving a note in product board for console changes so design/dev timelines align.

Maya: sgtm. we'll converge on hybrid routing + explicit per-customer datasets for regulated/high-volume customers. will finalize at weekly infra sync. :white_check_mark:
